sections.overview: Sparshall’s moth is an Australian notodontid found across several Australian states.
sections.identification: Adults span about 40 mm; females bear a tuft of hairs at the abdomen tip.
sections.habitat: The species account lists host trees but does not specify a habitat type.
sections.diet: Recorded larval food plants include Eucalyptus, Corymbia calophylla and Lophostemon confertus.
sections.behavior: Young larvae are gregarious; older ones are solitary.
sections.reproduction: It pupates in a cocoon in ground debris.
sections.ecology: The Atlas of Living Australia recognizes T. sparshalli as an accepted moth species and maps Australian occurrence records.
sections.conservation: The consulted accounts give no formal conservation assessment.
